summary: Intermittent asymmetric egress for EU-pinned traffic causing p95 latency spikes during autoscale
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (CatalystHealth) observed periodic increases in p95 token latency for EU-pinned requests (prod, eu-west). The spike correlates with cluster autoscale events (~04:15 UTC and ~11:30 UTC) when additional serving nodes come online. During these windows ~10-20% of requests that should remain in eu-west are observed egressing via us-west, adding ~80-250ms TLS/RTT overhead and causing p95 jumps.

Impact:
- Increased p95 latency to ~620-950ms for interactive chat endpoints for ~5-12 minute windows.
- Degraded UX for CatalystHealth's customers (enterprise SLA impacted).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod, eu-west region; customer pinned route policy: residency_mode=preferred (pin with TTL=10m).
- Affected model flavors: redwood-1.3-llama-compat (primary), open-llama-7b (fallback).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer issues large fan-out workload to eu-west pinned endpoint over 10 minutes to trigger autoscale.
2) Observe p95 via customer metrics and our Console -> Route Latency.
3) Correlate with control-plane scale events in the same time window.

Observed behavior:
- Traceroutes from serving runtime during incident show asymmetric hop: requests originate in eu-west but egress via NAT IPs mapped to us-west (see logs below).
- Control-plane routing logs show a 'route-refresh' coincident with node registration, during which route selection briefly allows cross-region fallback for a subset of sticky sessions.

Expected behavior:
- For residency_mode=preferred with active EU capacity available, traffic should remain within eu-west; fallback to other regions only when capacity or health checks fail. Route-refresh should not flip egress for pinned sessions during scale-in/scale-out windows.

Logs / metrics (excerpt):
- traceroute to 10.32.54.11 (serving node) -> final hop resolves to 34.203.x.x (us-west NAT) at 04:15:12 UTC
- control-plane event: scale_event id=se-98233 timestamp=2026-03-10T04:15:10Z action=node-register pool=eu-west nodes=+4
- routing decision log: route-select session=abcd1234 residency=preferred candidate_pool=[eu-west, us-west] selected=eu-west (control_plane:router) but egress_nat=us-west-nat-07 (network:egress)
- cloud flow logs: conn_count spike from eu-west LB to us-west NATs during event window

Preliminary investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: during node registration there is a short control-plane state reconciliation window where route pins and egress NAT assignment are evaluated asynchronously. Sticky session mapping (control-plane) remained pinned to eu-west but the path chosen by the network overlay selected a us-west egress for a subset of new connections created while the node came up.
- Repro steps executed on staging with scaled-down pool reproduced the asymmetric egress when we artificially delayed the control-plane's route-store update by ~3s.
- No evidence of customer misconfiguration; their route TTL/TTL-refresh is standard (10m).

Workaround applied:
- Support/CS temporarily advised CatalystHealth to set residency_mode=strict for the critical endpoints; that prevents cross-region egress at the cost of returning 429s during total EU capacity exhaustion. Customer accepted temporary change for the time being.

Next steps / planned fixes:
- Short term (SRE): implement a guard in control-plane:router to suppress non-deterministic egress reassignment for existing sticky sessions while node registration is in-progress (INT-7741). ETA: 48 hours for patch and targeted rollout to eu-west.
- Mid term (engineering): add egress-assignment atomic update (ensure NAT assignment is consistent with route pin atomically) and add an integration test covering autoscale + residency pins. PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2211
- Postmortem: schedule full incident review and update residency runbook with explicit autoscale handoff behavior.

Resolution / status:
- Workaround (strict residency) accepted and applied for affected routes at 2026-03-10T21:30:00Z. Engineering patch scheduled for rollout 2026-03-13. Monitoring alert created to detect asymmetric egress IPs and unpinned egress > 1% during scale windows.
